difficulty_reason: For a finite type morphism over an irreducible base, if the fibre over the generic point is not geometrically reduced then every fibre over a nonempty open fails to be geometrically reduced. The proof argues by contradiction using the spreading result for geometric reducedness: if some fibre in every neighbourhood were geometrically reduced, the spreading property would force the generic fibre to be geometrically reduced, contradicting the hypothesis. Using the positive spreading result to prove the negative statement is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 7188-7212.
